newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- Article calls for Chinese investors to be allowed to own and trade foreign-currency B-shares on the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets.
- Investigation shows that construction of huge Three Gorges dam project has so far caused no environmental damage.
- Beijing sells 11.4 billion yuan worth of non-tradeable bonds by end of May, meeting its target under national issue of 123 billion yuan.
- Total foreign investment in Beijing reaches $20.01 billion by end of April.
- Officials in southern Guangdong province burn 500 kg of illegal drugs to mark 158th anniversary of Chinese anti-narcotic action that sparked Opium War with Britain.
- Hong Kong firms sign accord with Tianjin port bonded zone to build China's largest classification centre for imported goods.
- Officials shut down petrochemical plant in Karamay in China's northwestern Xinjiang region because of pollution and financial losses.
- Computer network information centre set up to standardise management of sites on the Internet.
